newsitem.title: UK: Utd Biscuits sets new non-core disposals.
newsitem.headline: Utd Biscuits sets new non-core disposals.

text.p: British foods group United Biscuits Plc said on Wednesday that it was disposing of a number of business interests and taking action to withdraw from some low priority markets in a new series of moves designed to improve key businesses with the best prospects for profitable growth.
In a statement the company said the moves, some of which have already been completed, involved units with consolidated net sales of 42 million stg.
"Proceeds will amount to apporximately 10 milion stg," it added, saying it would take a non-operating exceptional charge of about 35 million stg in its 1996 accounts.
"The net effect of these actions will be modestly earnings enhancing," it added.

In addition, the company included a comment that its trading during the busy Christmas holiday period, when food spending in the company's main British and European markets picks up sharply, had been "satisfactory".
"UB therefore expects that the group's results for the year to December 28, 1996 will be as anticipated at the time of the interim results in September 1996," the company added.
UB said it had recently completed the sale of its 60 percent interest in an Italian snackfood producer, ICA Spa, to its management and a minority shareholder.

It had also completed the sale in October of its 84 percent interest in Portuguese snack business S&A Lda to Spain's Grefusa, and in December completed the sale of its 46 percent interest in Aguia SA, a Brazilian biscuit producer, to the majority shareholder.

It added that it had decided to withdraw from savoury snacks markets in Turkey and Hungary and would therefore be making a provision against the carrying value of its 30 percent interest in Turkey's Kargida and had closed a small snacks factory in Gyor, Hungary.

UB chief executive Eric Nicoli said that the steps, together with the recent disposals of Keebler and Ross Vegetable Products, represented "a very considerable tidying up and strengthening of our business portfolio and balance sheet".
"We now have a healthy balance of progressive established businesses and interests in emerging markets and we have a solid platform for future growth," he added.
